case_name: NPS 2009 Domain Exercise Users — Educational Forensic Corpus
executive_summary: Windows XP NTFS forensic image published by the Naval Postgraduate School (2009) as a public educational DFIR training corpus. Two scripted users (domex1, domex2) performed explicit exercise tasks (document creation, email, IM) under supervised conditions over 10 days (2008-10-20 to 2008-10-30). All artifacts are consistent with the documented exercise design: explicit exercise naming in file content, scripted timing, normal Shannon entropy (4.41), recoverable recycle bin files, scripted email/IM infrastructure. No anti-forensic indicators, no anomalous process activity, no cross-SID access violations. Chain of custody verified by 6 SHA-256 hashes. Verdict is NOISE — this is a training corpus, not a malicious incident.

peircean_analysis.firstness: FIWALK-001: 35313 file objects cataloged, NTFS partition, no unallocated deleted files, acquisition via fiwalk v0.5.1/TSK 3.0.0. USER-001: domex1 NTUSER.DAT hive, first login 2008-10-21 19:12 UTC, 16 restore point snapshots, 797 profile files. USER-002: domex2 NTUSER.DAT hive, first login 2008-10-21 19:29 UTC, DPAPI credential store created 2008-10-28 on first Outlook launch, 617 profile files. DOC-001: domex1 created 4 Office 2007 files in 152 seconds with explicit exercise names ('This is a word document by domex user 1.docx', 'This is a spreadsheet sent by domex user 1.xlsx'). Shannon entropy of creation sequence: 4.41 (normal plaintext range 4.0-5.0). REC-001: Dc3.docx and Dc4.xlsx in RECYCLER/SID-1003, ALLOC=1 (recoverable), not permanently deleted. EMAIL-001: domex2 Outlook 2007 with 3 PST files (Gmail, Hotmail, default), DPAPI-protected. IM-001: domex1 Pidgin IM (XMPP/Gmail/AIM), domex2 Pidgin (MSN/Gmail). SYS-001: 16 restore points over 10 days, pattern consistent with installation phase plus acquisition-triggered restore points. HASH-001: 6 artifacts hashed before analysis, no integrity violations.
peircean_analysis.secondness: The baseline for this corpus is an educational exercise: behavior is scripted, file names are explicit exercise labels, timing is artificial (4 files in 152 seconds by scripted user), and both user profiles were created within 17 minutes of each other (19:12 and 19:29 UTC) on the same day — consistent with supervised lab setup. Against this baseline: all observed behavior is exactly what the exercise design specifies. The 'anomalies' (short creation times, explicit naming) are not anomalies relative to the exercise design — they ARE the exercise design. Shannon entropy 4.41 is normal for Office document content. No process anomalies, no network connections to suspicious destinations, no anti-forensic tool signatures.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: This corpus was created to train DFIR analysts in artifact recovery and timeline reconstruction. The scripted behavior leaves deliberate forensic artifacts (Office docs, PST files, IM logs, recycle bin entries, LNK files) across all major Windows artifact categories, allowing students to practice the full recovery workflow. The naming convention ('by domex user 1', 'sent by domex user 1') explicitly labels each artifact for educational identification. The recycle bin files are left recoverable (ALLOC=1) — not permanently deleted — because the exercise requires students to recover them. All design choices are pedagogical, not operational.

caie.daubert: 2/8 artifacts structurally irrefutable (mft_entry spoofability=0.05, cryptographic_hash spoofability=0.05). Anchored in hard evidence. Admissible.
caie.highest_weighted: REC-001 (mft_entry, adjusted=0.0076) — NTFS MFT entries are structurally irrefutable (spoofability=0.05). ALLOC=1 status is machine-readable fact, not narrative claim.
caie.chain_of_custody_note: HASH-001 cryptographic chain (spoofability=0.05) provides the strongest anchor: 6 artifacts hashed before analysis, zero integrity violations.

corpus_context_analysis.acquisition_integrity: Image acquired 2008-10-30, fiwalk v0.5.1/TSK 3.0.0/AFF 3.3.4. SHA-256 verified. Write blocker used for original acquisition.
scripted_design_markers: Explicit exercise labels in file content ('This is a word document by domex user 1')
Both user accounts created within 17 minutes on the same day
DPAPI credential store created on first Outlook launch (2008-10-28) — first use, scripted scenario
Recycle bin files left recoverable (ALLOC=1) — pedagogical design, not cleanup failure
Shannon entropy 4.41 — normal document content, no packing or obfuscation
16 restore points: RP1-RP5 in first 3 hours (setup), RP6 on first domex snapshot, RP10-RP16 on acquisition day

hypotheses.H1_malicious_insider: domex1 or domex2 conducted actual malicious activity disguised as a training exercise.
hypotheses.H2_educational_corpus: All artifacts are the expected output of a scripted DFIR training exercise, published by NPS for educational use.

refutation_protocol.benign_hypothesis: H2 (educational corpus) — this IS the expected benign explanation for this corpus.
refutation_protocol.test_result: H1 REFUTED: (A) File naming convention ('This is a word document by domex user 1.docx') is explicit exercise labeling — no malicious actor labels their operational documents with their scripted identity. (B) All 4 documents created and deleted within 152 seconds — this is exercise task completion speed, not operational tempo. (C) No anti-forensic tool signatures in the 35313 file objects. (D) No cross-SID access — domex1 files stayed in SID-1003 space, domex2 in SID-1004. No lateral movement between user accounts. (E) Recycle bin files ALLOC=1 — a malicious user covering tracks would have permanently deleted exfiltrated documents, not left them recoverable in the bin.
refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H1 REFUTED on five independent prongs. H2 confirmed. Verdict: NOISE.

devil_advocate: A sophisticated insider threat could use an exercise corpus as operational cover — performing real malicious activity alongside the scripted tasks, knowing forensic reviewers would attribute everything to the exercise. In this corpus: no evidence of activity outside the documented exercise scope. No anomalous network connections, no unexpected process execution, no files outside the exercise user directories, no timestamps outside the 10-day exercise window. The explicit labeling convention and 100% coverage of expected exercise artifacts leave no residual unexplained activity.

findings.title: Educational Training Corpus — No Malicious Activity
findings.firstness: 35313 files, two scripted users, 10-day exercise, explicit naming, normal entropy
findings.secondness: All artifacts consistent with documented NPS exercise design; no unexplained residuals
findings.thirdness: Pedagogical corpus by Naval Postgraduate School — design choices are educational, not operational
findings.devil_advocate: Could be used as cover for real insider activity — refuted by absence of any out-of-scope artifacts
findings.corroboration: Public corpus (NPS Digital Corpora, documented online) — external reference independently confirms the exercise design

known_limitations: DPAPI master key (domex2) protects credential material — Outlook PST email content not decrypted. Content of exercise emails not verified.
Pidgin IM conversation logs not extracted — IM session content not reviewed.
Only 8 representative artifacts analyzed — 35313 total file objects not individually processed.
